question: Can joint, continuous experiences teach a single graph both private triangular odors and context-dependent foraging? Does interleaving the two kinds of support help?
training: Same original or independent 64k nonlinear graph for both arms. In every training life actually visit seven supports: three private triangular odor pairs, two scene backgrounds assigning value to the same odor, and the positive and negative feeder demonstrations. Then take two consecutive actions, one chosen object from each skill, in random order. Neither action sees a terminal taste before the second decision. The only outer reward is 1 if both resources were physically selected successfully. All seven displayed supports share one set of hidden activities, eligibility traces and writable parameters. No private law, domain tag or correct side enters the circuit.
pair: Blocked: the three odor supports precede or follow the four context/feeder supports with equal probability. Interspersed: the same object-bound overlaps, private laws, study choices' random numbers and neutral waits are alternated. Advance the pre-contact waits including the first, so total support time is identical in every matched world. Same two sampled terminal questions, order and motor/edit uniforms. No reversal of a completed life for replay; the environment owns all sampling.
budget: 8000 outer updates, each using four independent world roots per birth and four randomly sampled private maps paired with their complements. Both arms start fresh Adam at the same inherited body, optimize all usual inherited weights, biases and rules, and retain all lifetime weight, bias and topology changes within each experience.
evaluation: Use the existing same-lifetime six-way common snapshot benchmark at a fixed intermediate and the terminal stage, and a separate disjoint world bank at the final stage. Measure actual two-action terminal reward on untouched worlds too. Report all maps, A/B conflict and difficult triangles combined with conflicts. Keep components and six-way success separate. The previous alternating-development study uses a different amount and organization of experience; do not claim its comparison isolates a single training factor.
